initiative.title: Notebook analysis with synchronized definitions
initiative.summary: Interleave prose, dashboard-language blocks, and editable graphics in one reading column. Preserve both edit directions. Eleven researched examples inform the next scope decisions.
initiative.next_action: Choose the first reproduction (forecast performance is recommended) and its relationship to saved dashboard views, then shape the edit-and-reopen proof.

sources.anchor: Okay, let's go ahead and create a new intent document around the desire to produce an output that looks more like a notebook-style execution where we've got text and graphics interleaved. In particular, the goal is to go after something that feels a little bit more like observable rather than the These things which are straight dashboard. And what I'd really like to uncover is ways to define the queries and basically the visuals that result using our dashboarding language and to have it be kind of two-way synced so that the user can edit the graphs after they're made and then that persists back into the like text that defines the calculation block. And basically to just have the notebook style thing be just another coherent view into the rest of the features of the application. So go ahead and capture that as an intent. And then in the intent document, include 10 questions that would be good to answer to dial in the scope
Complete-dashboard declarations; calculations; chart-local where filters; compileDocument/exportDocument; compileViews/exportViews.

claims.statement: Read explanation, calculation blocks, and graphics as one ordered notebook analysis.
Use Observable as an experience reference for interleaved analysis.
claims.notes: No syntax, runtime, hosting, or collaboration requirement is inferred.

claims.statement: Use the dashboard language to define queries, calculations, and resulting visuals.
claims.notes: Required query breadth is unresolved; current declarations may not cover it.

claims.statement: Text edits update results, and graphical edits persist into the text defining the corresponding block.
claims.notes: Supported edit types, update timing, and treatment of invalid drafts remain open.

claims.statement: The notebook is another coherent view into existing explorEDA capabilities.
claims.notes: Whether notebook and dashboard share saved-view identity remains open.

claims.statement: Saved work retains the meaning of definitions and graphs when reopened.
claims.notes: Derived from edits persisting back into block text. Export and sharing are not settled.

claims.statement: The likely author investigates data and explains the reasoning to a reader.
claims.notes: The user did not select a first audience or task.

claims.statement: Dashboard text already compiles and exports saved settings, including calculations and multiple views.
claims.notes: These APIs do not prove preservation of authored notebook blocks, comments, or formatting.

claims.statement: The current Markdown panel stores rich text without notebook execution.
Create an intent document with ten scope questions; do not start shaping or implementation in this request.
claims.notes: The explicit ten-question request overrides the skill default of three.

claims.statement: Interleave text, calculations, and graphics in one reading column; each main block spans that column.
claims.notes: Individual graphics may contain facets. The reading sequence is not a grid of unrelated dashboard panels.

human_questions.question: Who will author and read the first notebook, and what real analysis should they complete?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets the primary workflow and reader needs.
human_questions.research_context: The collection offers investigative, teaching, and published narrative examples. It does not choose the first author or reader.

human_questions.question: What is the smallest useful version: prose, definition blocks, and one chart, or tables and summary values too?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets the first release boundary and appetite.
human_questions.research_context: Forecast performance is the recommended small candidate. This is not a user-approved first release.

human_questions.question: Are current dashboard declarations enough initially, or must blocks produce named results that later blocks can use?
human_questions.decision_impact: Determines whether reusable intermediate outputs are needed.
human_questions.research_context: Forecast uses a small derived field. Date Patterns and Seattle need broader intermediate computations; related-table queries already exist.

human_questions.question: Should changes run automatically, require running one block, or require running the whole notebook?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets when results refresh and what execution controls users need.
human_questions.research_context: Source examples include reactive controls, static authored outputs, and explicit randomized runs. There is no single implied execution policy.

human_questions.question: Should calculations and interactive filters affect the whole notebook, only later blocks, or explicitly linked blocks?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets population and dependency expectations across blocks.
human_questions.research_context: Date Patterns demonstrates a local brush independent of later grouping. Correlation mixes local controls with shared styling.

human_questions.question: Which edits must write back first: fields, chart type, aggregation, filters, axis settings, or visual styling?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets the first supported graphical write-back contract.
human_questions.research_context: The report proposes many graphical edits; observed source controls are distinguished. The first write-back coverage is still open.

human_questions.question: Must graph edits preserve comments, formatting, and declaration order, or is regenerated equivalent text acceptable?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets whether equivalent generated text is sufficient.
human_questions.research_context: The current exporter regenerates text from settings. Research does not resolve comment and formatting preservation expectations.

human_questions.question: Is the notebook another presentation of the same saved dashboard, or a separate document that reuses its analysis objects?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets saved-view identity and cross-view edit expectations.
human_questions.research_context: Shared data does not establish whether notebook and dashboard share one saved view.

human_questions.question: While block text is invalid, should the last valid graph remain editable, and how should users reconcile those edits?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets visible behavior when draft text and valid graphical state differ.
human_questions.research_context: Broken source branches demonstrate scoped failures. They do not settle how invalid drafts and graph edits should coexist.

human_questions.question: Is reopening an editable notebook enough initially, or must users also share or export a readable, self-contained result?
human_questions.decision_impact: Sets persistence, sharing, and export expectations.
human_questions.research_context: The offline research report is a delivery format, not evidence that notebook export is required in the first release.

shape_readiness.reason: Research identifies concrete reproduction candidates. Audience, first-release appetite, execution, text preservation, and saved-view identity remain open.

recommendation.simpler_alternative: Arrange existing rich-text and chart panels in one column to test reading flow. This alone cannot prove definition write-back.
recommendation.proof: One prepared source, a named delta calculation, full-series and local-window outputs. Edit text and graphical settings, then save and reopen.
recommendation.observation: The same calculation and output survive both edit directions; local changes leave the earlier full-series result intact.
recommendation.decision_rule: Expand only when definitions and outputs agree after both edit paths and reopening. Revisit the design if authored blocks or calculation meaning drift.
recommendation.prerequisite: Obtain and audit the forecast CSV; reconcile units, timestamps, missing rows, and duplicate hours before fixing expected outputs.

implications.statement: Separate reading order from execution dependencies.
Distinguish local domains, shared filters, grouping inputs, and shared style.
Preserve formulas and population meaning during graphical editing.
Separate computed narrative values from authored conclusions.
Keep errors and stale results scoped to affected outputs.
Make raw rows, transformed rows, and chart values distinguishable.

verification_limits: The source index and original synthesis were reviewed for all eleven examples. Three representative screenshots were visually inspected locally.
Upstream pages, datasets, controls, and calculations were not independently rerun during this synthesis.
The package contains no upstream datasets. The Pro report marks several attached-data claims as loaded rows rather than independently downloaded bytes.
Repository documentation and selected code were read. No application reproduction or browser feature test was performed.
Original report-generation code was preserved without execution.
